entries.threat: missing or expired session
entries.setup: Build a request with no valid session and no capture token.
entries.attack: Invoke every protected route method.
entries.expected: Reject before repository access with the matrix-defined unauthenticated response.

entries.threat: cross-tenant identifier guessing
entries.setup: Create the resource for alpha and authenticate as beta.
entries.attack: Read, update, or delete alpha's identifier as beta.
entries.expected: Return the same not-found response as an unknown identifier and make no mutation.

entries.threat: mixed-tenant parent and child identifiers
entries.setup: Create a collection for alpha and an item for beta.
entries.attack: Attach beta's item to alpha's collection, and try the inverse combination.
entries.expected: Reject both combinations without revealing which identifier belongs to another tenant.

entries.surface: all tenant repository reads and mutations
entries.threat: omitted tenant predicate
entries.setup: Seed colliding business identifiers and distinguishable records for alpha and beta.
entries.attack: Execute every repository method using alpha's AuthContext.
entries.expected: Only alpha's rows are returned or mutated; tenant context is mandatory at the call boundary.

entries.threat: repository regression or raw SQL missing a tenant predicate
entries.setup: Insert one row per tenant and use the restricted application database role.
entries.attack: Select, update, and delete beta's row while the transaction-local tenant is alpha.
entries.expected: RLS hides beta's row and prevents mutation even when application SQL is incorrectly broad.

entries.threat: tenant context leaking between checked-out connections
entries.setup: Use a single-connection pool and alternate alpha, beta, and context-free transactions.
entries.attack: Query after each checkout and after a failed transaction.
entries.expected: Each transaction sees only its tenant and no tenant setting remains after commit or rollback.

entries.threat: forged CaptureQueueMessageV2 tenant
entries.setup: Create a capture for alpha and forge a syntactically valid envelope naming beta.
entries.attack: Deliver the forged envelope directly to the consumer.
entries.expected: Reject the tenant-resource mismatch and perform no fetch, item write, or status transition.

entries.threat: forged TenantJobEnvelopeV1 tenant or legacy unscoped payload
entries.setup: Create a job for alpha and build the forged fixtures from tests/support/phase3-tenancy.ts.
entries.attack: Deliver wrong-version, missing-context, and beta-for-alpha envelopes.
entries.expected: Reject before resolving a handler and preserve the original job unchanged.

entries.threat: cross-tenant retrieval through an index
entries.setup: Give beta a uniquely searchable marker absent from alpha's data.
entries.attack: Search for beta's marker as alpha, including filters and pagination cursors.
entries.expected: Return no beta identifiers, snippets, counts, facets, or cursor information.

entries.threat: cross-tenant document assembled into an AI prompt
entries.setup: Give beta a unique canary string and capture outbound provider inputs.
entries.attack: Ask alpha a question designed to retrieve beta's canary.
entries.expected: The provider input, citations, persisted artifacts, and response contain no beta data.

entries.threat: cache key missing tenant identity
entries.setup: Warm a cache as alpha using the same non-tenant inputs beta will request.
entries.attack: Repeat the request as beta.
entries.expected: Beta cannot receive alpha's cached value; tenant identity is part of every private cache key.

entries.threat: one tenant consuming or bypassing another tenant's quota
entries.setup: Exhaust alpha's limit while beta has the same network address and request shape.
entries.attack: Request as beta, then rotate alpha's token while preserving alpha ownership.
entries.expected: Beta retains its quota and alpha cannot evade a user-scoped quota by rotating credentials.

entries.threat: tenant data leakage through observability
entries.setup: Use alpha and beta canaries in resource bodies, tokens, and query strings.
entries.attack: Exercise failures, retries, authorization denials, and AI-provider errors.
entries.expected: Logs have request and tenant correlation but contain no secrets or other tenant's content.

entries.surface: raw content, exports, and future media objects
entries.threat: guessable storage key or cross-tenant signed URL
entries.setup: Store an object for alpha and authenticate as beta.
entries.attack: Request the object key directly and replay any previously issued signed URL.
entries.expected: Deny access; private keys include an immutable tenant boundary and signed URLs are narrowly scoped.

entries.threat: replayed invite causes email flooding or duplicate account activation
entries.setup: Prepare one valid invitation and one verified provider session.
entries.attack: Concurrently request the magic link twice and replay the same completion state twice.
entries.expected: Exactly one provider dispatch and one account activation occur; all replays are generic denials.

entries.surface: every cookie-authenticated owner mutation generated from the authorization matrix
entries.threat: cross-site request forgery after enabling Neon Auth
entries.setup: Authenticate alpha and enumerate every POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE owner surface.
entries.attack: Invoke each surface with a missing or hostile Origin while preserving alpha's session cookie.
entries.expected: Return 403 before repository, provider, queue, or object-store side effects.

entries.surface: session/device listing, targeted revocation, and account disable
entries.threat: session substitution, token disclosure, or stale access after revocation
entries.setup: Give alpha two devices, beta one device, and retain their provider session tokens only server-side.
entries.attack: Guess beta's device id, revoke alpha's second device, and disable alpha during an active request.
entries.expected: Tokens are never returned; foreign ids are concealed; revoked or disabled sessions fail the next protected request.

entries.surface: connector OAuth state issue and consume
entries.threat: open redirect, provider substitution, replay, or cross-tenant nonce burn
entries.setup: Issue alpha state bound to alpha's session and Gmail.
entries.attack: Consume as beta, consume as Slack, use a backslash external return path, then replay as alpha.
entries.expected: Invalid attempts cannot burn alpha's state; return remains same-origin; only alpha/Gmail succeeds exactly once.

entries.surface: account export builder and stored artifact
entries.threat: denylist gaps leak credentials, another tenant, or future unreviewed tables
entries.setup: Seed alpha and beta content plus token, cookie, OAuth, prompt, and URL canaries.
entries.attack: Build alpha's export and recursively inspect every key and value.
entries.expected: Only explicit allowlisted sections exist; alpha content is present; credentials, internal hashes, and beta canaries are absent.

entries.threat: foreign export-id guessing or stale artifact replay
entries.setup: Complete alpha's export and prepare an unknown export id.
entries.attack: Read/download as beta, after expiry, and after alpha deletion.
entries.expected: Foreign and missing ids are identical 404s; expired/deleted artifacts cannot be downloaded.

entries.threat: orphaned rows, credentials, jobs, or objects after deletion
entries.setup: Seed the full alpha ownership graph and an independent beta graph.
entries.attack: Delete alpha and inspect every reviewed table, queue, connector, and object seam.
entries.expected: Alpha access is revoked before purge, the full alpha graph is gone, and beta is byte-for-byte unchanged.

entries.surface: deletion request, cancellation, and worker race
entries.threat: capture/job commit races deletion or cancellation races irreversible purge
entries.setup: Pause deletion at each checkpoint with in-flight tenant jobs and a deterministic barrier.
entries.attack: Interleave request, auth, enqueue, retry, cancellation, duplicate delivery, and worker restart.
entries.expected: No new personal work commits after disable; cancellation is bounded to the reversible state; replay resumes idempotently.

entries.surface: capture, export, deletion, and durable-job retry
entries.threat: duplicate delivery or retry changes tenant or repeats effects
entries.setup: Prepare one valid message, an exact duplicate, a retry, and a forged-owner copy.
entries.attack: Deliver all messages concurrently and again after a simulated process restart.
entries.expected: One logical effect occurs; retry preserves tenant; duplicate is idempotent; forgery has no effect.

entries.surface: concurrent tenant transactions through a small PostgreSQL pool
entries.threat: RLS context crossover under pool pressure
entries.setup: Use more alpha/beta operations than pool connections with colliding public identifiers.
entries.attack: Run reads, writes, commit, rollback, and cancellation in randomized but seeded order.
entries.expected: Every result belongs to the caller and every checked-in connection has empty tenant settings.

entries.surface: feed, search, export, and deletion query plans
entries.threat: tenant predicate applied after a broad scan or ranking stage
entries.setup: Seed realistic alpha/beta cardinality and collect stable EXPLAIN plans without ANALYZE.
entries.attack: Inspect candidate, join, rank, and delete plans for each reviewed query family.
entries.expected: The tenant predicate is visible at the earliest relation and tenant-leading indexes are usable.

entries.threat: outage leaves downloadable partial export or unrecoverable partial deletion
entries.setup: Inject a one-shot failure before and after each database/object-store checkpoint.
entries.attack: Restart the worker and redeliver the same message.
entries.expected: Partial exports are never downloadable; workers resume or safely repeat; completed evidence is durable.

entries.surface: auth provider, database, queue, and object-store seams
entries.threat: dependency outage widens authorization or loses accepted work
entries.setup: Configure deterministic one-shot failures at named external-effect boundaries.
entries.attack: Exercise login, export, deletion, and retry across each injected failure.
entries.expected: Authorization fails closed; accepted work remains durable; retries do not duplicate effects.

entries.surface: committed production package manifest and lock graph
entries.threat: unpinned auth SDK, incompatible peers, or unapproved reciprocal license
entries.setup: Read only package.json and package-lock.json with no registry access.
entries.attack: Check the exact auth SDK pin, locked version, Better Auth peer resolution, and every production license.
entries.expected: The graph is deterministic, peer-compatible, and contains no unapproved AGPL dependency.
